description: Gold Claim Ledger for forge_explore benchmark evaluation. Each claim has verifiable ground truth, expected source class, permitted wording constraints, and a difficulty level. Used to score any exploration tool against a common standard.

claims.proposition: Kurt Gödel published his incompleteness theorems in 1931
The first incompleteness theorem states: any consistent formal system capable of expressing basic arithmetic is incomplete — there exist true statements within it that cannot be proved
claims.permitted_wording: consistent formal system / cannot be proved / undecidable / incomplete
claims.forbidden_wording: all systems are incomplete / mathematics is broken / proves nothing

claims.proposition: π (pi) is an irrational number — it cannot be expressed as a fraction of two integers
claims.permitted_wording: irrational / cannot be expressed as a fraction / Lambert proved

claims.proposition: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, leading to German reunification
claims.permitted_wording: fell on November 9, 1989 / opened on November 9, 1989 / border opened
claims.forbidden_wording: destroyed / torn down completely that day (gradual demolition followed)

claims.proposition: The Apollo 11 mission landed humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969; Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the lunar surface
expected_sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
claims.permitted_wording: landed July 20, 1969 / Armstrong first on surface / Apollo 11

claims.proposition: World War II in Europe ended with Germany's unconditional surrender on May 8, 1945 (VE Day)
claims.permitted_wording: May 8, 1945 / unconditional surrender / VE Day / Germany surrendered
claims.forbidden_wording: May 7 (different time zone / different signing) — unless qualified

claims.proposition: At standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm), pure water boils at 100°C (212°F)
claims.permitted_wording: at standard pressure / at sea level / 100°C / 212°F

claims.proposition: The Earth orbits the Sun (heliocentrism); this was proposed by Copernicus (1543) and supported by Galileo's observations
claims.permitted_wording: Earth orbits Sun / Copernicus 1543 / Galileo observed / heliocentric model
claims.forbidden_wording: discovered by Galileo / first proposed by Galileo

claims.proposition: The structure of DNA is a double helix, first described by Watson and Crick in 1953, building on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray crystallography
claims.permitted_wording: Watson and Crick 1953 / double helix / Franklin contributed crystallography
claims.forbidden_wording: Watson and Crick alone discovered / Franklin irrelevant

claims.proposition: The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic on March 11, 2020
claims.permitted_wording: March 11, 2020 / WHO declared pandemic / global pandemic
claims.forbidden_wording: March 2020 (without specific date) / epidemic / WHO created

claims.proposition: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on December 25, 2021, on an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana
claims.permitted_wording: December 25, 2021 / Ariane 5 / French Guiana / JWST launched
claims.forbidden_wording: Hubble replacement (different mission class) / December 2021 (without date)

claims.proposition: The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye
claims.permitted_wording: popular myth / not visible to naked eye / requires magnification / astronauts report not visible
claims.adversarial_note: This is a widely-repeated FALSE claim. A good tool must find sources that DEBUNK it, not just sources that repeat it.

claims.proposition: Vitamin C supplementation prevents the common cold
expected_sources: Cochrane Review (2013): 'Vitamin C does not reduce incidence but may reduce duration'
claims.permitted_wording: does not prevent / may reduce duration / evidence mixed / Pauling claimed but evidence limited
claims.forbidden_wording: proven to prevent / definitely prevents / proven ineffective
claims.adversarial_note: DISPUTED claim. Correct answer: prevention NOT proven; may reduce symptom duration. Tool must show BOTH sides and label uncertainty correctly.

claims.proposition: The philosopher René Descartes wrote 'Cogito, ergo sum' (I think, therefore I am) in his 1637 work 'Discourse on the Method'
expected_sources: Discourse on the Method (1637), Part IV
claims.permitted_wording: Discourse on the Method 1637 / Part IV / Latin formulation / French: 'Je pense, donc je suis'
claims.forbidden_wording: Meditations (1641 — also contains similar idea but 'Cogito' first appears in Discourse)
claims.adversarial_note: Common confusion: 'Cogito' appears in Discourse (1637) in French, later in Meditations (1641) in Latin. Tool must get the primary source right.

claims.proposition: The US Supreme Court case Brown v. Board of Education (1954) unanimously declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional, overturning Plessy v. Ferguson (1896)
expected_sources: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954)
claims.permitted_wording: 347 U.S. 483 / unanimous 9-0 / overturned Plessy / 'separate but equal' unconstitutional
claims.forbidden_wording: ended all segregation immediately (implementation followed later) / 1955

usage: Score each track (A/B/C/D) against this ledger. For each claim, evaluate: (1) Did the tool find the claim? (2) Did it cite the right source class? (3) Did it use permitted wording and avoid forbidden wording? (4) Did it correctly label epistemic status? Record raw results per claim. Compute aggregate metrics only after all tracks have been scored independently.
status: DRAFT — not yet validated against live retrieval
